::: {.column width="55%" .tight}
**A: Concert**

- Graphic score [*DISCOUNT*](https://hvc.berlin/discount/) deployed to all nodes 
- Players read the score on their node
- Video nodes show it to the audience
- Performers spread through the room

::: {.sw-head}
**B: Interactive installation**
:::

- A camera at every node tracks audience
- OpenCV: pixel entropy as main parameter
- Screens show the motion field back to visitors
- Movement sonified on all nodes (OSC)
:::
::::

::: prose
At the Convergence Innovation Competition Asia, MËSH ran in two modes: a concert and an interactive installation.

In performance mode, MËSH supported a networked ensemble in which performers controlled their own audio streams. The graphic score *DISCOUNT* was deployed to all nodes simultaneously with Ansible: musicians read it on the touchscreen at their node while the video nodes displayed it for the audience. Wireless connectivity let performers, and the sound, fill the room.

In installation mode, visitors interacted through a camera at each node. A Python/OpenCV script tracked total pixel movement as a proxy for people moving through the room; each node's data was shared over OSC and used as control data for a SuperCollider sound field. Each touchscreen showed the direction every pixel moved between frames, inviting visitors to find out how their active and passive movement changed the sound field.
:::
